children: UBS Global Wealth Management now expects the Federal Reserve to keep raising interest rates into
March 2027
, extending the tightening cycle after September inflation came in stronger than expected.
The call marks a meaningful shift in the rate outlook.
The Fed raised rates by
25 basis points in September
, its first increase since 2023. UBS expects another quarter-point increase in
December
, followed by a third hike in
March 2027
The combination of stronger goods inflation with strong services inflation supports a higher-for-longer Fed outlook, UBS economist Andrew Dubinsky said.
The latest CPI report appears to have strengthened the case.

September inflation showed broader price pressures than markets had expected, reinforcing concerns that the Fed may need to remain restrictive for longer rather than treating the latest inflation bump as temporary.
UBS also pointed to several outside forces that could keep inflation elevated.
Those include
AI-driven demand, Middle East-related supply disruptions and trade-policy uncertainty
, all of which could keep pressure on prices even if other parts of the economy cool.
The longer tightening cycle is designed to ensure inflation expectations stay anchored while inflation remains near 3% due to overlapping shocks, UBS said.
Markets are already adjusting.
Interest-rate futures now imply roughly a
27% chance of a Fed hike at the October 2728 meeting
, up from 21.6% before the CPI report, while the probability of a December hike has climbed to about
, according to CME FedWatch data.
Investor Takeaway
I think the bigger market implication is that the debate is moving beyond whether the Fed hikes again this year.
The more important question is whether the tightening cycle now
bleeds into 2027
That matters because a March hike would keep borrowing costs elevated for longer across mortgages, corporate debt and equity valuations.
It would also challenge the idea that markets can quickly return to a lower-rate environment after the recent inflation shock.
For investors, the key things to watch are
core inflation, services prices, wage growth, inflation expectations and the Fed's October and December guidance
If inflation stays near 3% and supply-side pressures persist, UBS's call suggests the market may need to price in a longer period of restrictive monetary policy than many investors had expected.

title: UBS Sees a Major Economic Twist After Inflation Shock
